subject: Clarify purchasing model fit & payflow
messages:
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@storify.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Quick follow-up after demo — purchasing path questions

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning — the latency examples and the dedupe caching callout were particularly helpful for the team. A couple of procurement-oriented questions we promised to clarify on our side and thought it would be helpful to get those answers from you before we loop in our procurement/legal team: \n
1) Packaging/hosting fit: if we start with Hosted (API) on an on-demand plan, what is the path/discount if we later move to Dedicated (reserved GPU) with a commit? Conversely, how different is the paperwork for Private deployment?

2) Purchase route: does Redwood accept PO (net-45/60) for Dedicated and Private? Do you support AWS Marketplace procurement (SaaS/subscription) and if so how does that affect committed pricing?

3) Billing artifacts: for our internal vendor intake we need an invoice template and confirmation of whether sandbox/dev usage can be consolidated on the same invoice as production.

4) Timeline: our procurement lead time is typically 30–45 days for PO approval. Are there short-term bridging options (e.g., credit card for initial onboarding) you recommend?

If you can send a short note that I can forward to our procurement team (including a simple matrix of hosting option vs. purchase route vs. paperwork required), that would unblock next steps.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Reed
Head of ML Platforms — Storify.ai
alex.reed@storify.ai
+1 (650) 555-0143

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@storify.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — purchasing path questions

Hi Alex — great questions, thanks for laying them out. Per our call and the internal follow-up with finance, here is a concise matrix you can share with your procurement team (short answers first, details below):

- Hosted (Redwood API)
  * Purchase routes: Credit card (immediate), PO (net-30 or net-45 on approved accounts), Marketplace (AWS)
  * Pricing: on-demand per-token/embedding rates; 12/24-month commits available for discount tiers
  * Paperwork: standard SaaS MSA + order form when PO required; invoice frequency monthly

- Dedicated (reserved capacity)
  * Purchase routes: PO (preferred for committed capacity), credit card for trials only
  * Pricing: monthly committed spend with throughput tiers; discounts applied for 12/24-month commitments
  * Paperwork: enterprise contract + SOW; invoices deliverable monthly or quarterly per agreement

- Private (VPC/on-prem)
  * Purchase routes: PO only; requires procurement + security approvals
  * Pricing: platform fee + baseline committed capacity; one-time setup professional services
  * Paperwork: enterprise licensing agreement, SOW, security annex (SOC2 evidence available)

Notes and answers to your specific points:
1) Path/discounts: Moving from Hosted on-demand to a Dedicated commit is a normal progression. We typically credit up to the first 30 days of prepaid usage against the Dedicated commitment if signed within 90 days. Committed discounts are 15–25% for 12 months and 25–35% for 24 months (depend on throughput tier).

2) PO and Marketplace: We accept POs for Hosted (for approved accounts), Dedicated, and Private. AWS Marketplace is supported for Hosted SaaS subscriptions; pricing on Marketplace excludes certain sales credits/partner discounts, so we normally run parity pricing or a small premium — we can present both options.

3) Billing artifacts: I attached a simple pricing grid (pricing_grid_q2_2027.xlsx) and an invoice sample. Sandbox/dev usage can be consolidated on a single invoice, but some customers prefer separate billing line items — both are possible.

4) Bridging options: recommend using a credit-card-backed trial or short-term month-to-month contract while PO is processed; we can provision Dedicated trial nodes for 2–4 weeks to validate throughput.

Next steps I propose:
- I will prepare two short options for procurement (Direct PO + Enterprise SOW, and AWS Marketplace subscription) with sample contract language and an initial pricing snapshot for Dedicated 2× and 4× throughput tiers.
- Could you confirm: procurement lead name and email, preferred PO terms (net-30/net-45), and whether a Marketplace purchase is acceptable?

If you want, I can also tee up a quick call with Monica (commercial lead) and our finance contacts to walk procurement through the paperwork.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
Attachment: pricing_grid_q2_2027.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — purchasing path questions (internal)

Evelyn / Ben — internal note on commercial levers we can present to Storify: 

- Pricing bands: propose publishing two example offers: (A) Hosted SaaS on Marketplace (standard list) and (B) Direct PO with committed Dedicated discount. For (B) include 12m @ -18% and 24m @ -28% as starting points; we can lean on partner credits for enterprise customers if they buy marketplace + reserved.
- PO terms: if they need net-45 we can approve net-45 for this account with finance sign-off (deal desk required).
- Trial bridging: offer 30-day CC trial for Hosted; Dedicated trials should be timeboxed and limited to a subset of capacity.
- Attachments to include when we send to procurement: pricing grid, sample MSA + SOW template, invoice sample, SOC2 summary.

Recommend we draft two short PDFs (one-page each): (1) PO path: Direct purchase + SOW summary + proposed committed pricing, (2) Marketplace path: subscription terms + onboarding checklist. I can draft both — want to confirm on discount bands before sending.

If Ben agrees to the 12/24 bands above, I'll assemble and we can send to Alex to forward to procurement.

- Monica
Monica Patel
Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Lisa Morgan <lisa.morgan@storify.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Alex Reed <alex.reed@storify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — purchasing path questions

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the clear matrix and the pricing grid. A few procurement items from our side: 

1) Purchase route: Storify prefers to pay via PO (we can do net-45) for any multi-month committed purchase. For immediate test/proof-of-concept we will use a company card.

2) Timeline: our procurement approval (legal + vendor intake) typically takes 30–45 days; we'll open a PR and push to get the PO started this week.

3) Requirements: attaching a short doc with our vendor intake checklist (storify_procurement_requirements.pdf). Important points: SOC2 report access, sample invoice, W-9, and a primary contact for billing ops. If you can confirm SOC2 host location and whether you support VAT/withholding adjustments on invoices, that would help.

4) Desired commercial shape: our engineering lead prefers Dedicated with a 12-month commit for predictable latency; please provide two pricing rows (Dedicated 2×, Dedicated 4×) with monthly commitment, and confirm if Redwood will accept a net-45 PO at the proposed committed discount bands. Also confirm whether Marketplace parity will be possible if we choose that route.

Alex will coordinate procurement; his procurement contact is lisa.morgan@storify.ai (that's me). Please send the two one-pagers Monica suggested and a sample order form.

Best regards,
Lisa Morgan
CFO | Storify.ai
lisa.morgan@storify.ai
Attachment: storify_procurement_requirements.pdf (1 page checklist)
